=== INDIA TODAY - INDIA NEWS (August 20, 2026) ===

1. GOODBYE NIKETU IRALU: PEACE ICON WHO EMERGED FROM CRADLE OF NAGA ARMED REBELLION
Nagaland today bid adieu to iconic peace activist Niketu Iralu who died this week. For over six decades, Iralu had been offering a healing touch to the fractured Naga society. He was born in Khonoma, the same village where Angami Zapu Phizo, father of Naga insurgency, was born. Iralu was related to Phizo but took a very different path.

2. DEAD RAT FOUND IN BRANDED NAMKEEN PACKET IN KANPUR DEHAT; FOOD SAFETY DEPARTMENT ISSUES NOTICE
A serious food safety concern has emerged from Kanpur Dehat after a dead rat was reportedly discovered inside a sealed packet of Bikanervala Navratna mixture namkeen. The packet, purchased at a grocery store on Mughal Road, prompted immediate outrage and demands for a strict investigation regarding hygiene standards. Following a formal complaint and viral video of the incident, the Food and Safety Department in Uttar Pradesh issued a notice to the manufacturer. Officials sent a regional food safety inspection team to conduct an on-spot investigation, record witness statements, and question company representatives to enforce compliance with food safety laws.

3. ABHIJEET DIPKE SEEKS MAHARASHTRA MINISTER'S RESIGNATION OVER CRUMBLING SCHOOLS
After inspecting a school in Latur, Abhijeet Dipke demanded Maharashtra Education Minister Dada Bhuse's resignation over poor facilities.

4. YOU FACED IT ALL SINCE PAPA LEFT: RAHUL'S TRIBUTE TO SONIA BEFORE MEMOIR RELEASE
On former PM Rajiv Gandhi's anniversary, Congress MP Rahul Gandhi said he is proud that his mother Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be read by millions of readers. The memoir is set to be released on November 10.

5. RTO BEGINS MARATHI PROFICIENCY TEST FOR AUTO DRIVERS IN THANE; NON-COMPLIANT DRIVERS SERVED NOTICES
The Regional Transport Office in Thane, Maharashtra, has initiated checks on auto-rickshaw and taxi drivers to assess their working knowledge of the Marathi language. Under the Maharashtra Motor Vehicles Rules, Marathi proficiency is compulsory for obtaining commercial driving licenses and badges. During the drive, officials test drivers on basic Marathi skills. Drivers unable to speak or understand the language are being issued notices requiring them to acquire working knowledge within one month. The mandate has sparked debate among transport unions, who previously protested against verifying existing license holders, citing concerns over language politics.

6. OPPOSITION LEADER TARGETS GOVERNMENT, RSS OVER STUDENT ISSUES; CONGRESS PLANS GEN Z OUTREACH
The Leader of Opposition launched a sharp attack against the government and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh over student issues and the centralization of power. The opposition party alleged that the system is attempting to control and attack students rather than listening to their concerns. Furthermore, criticisms were raised against the central governing model, citing the monopolization of business and resources that hinders self-reliance. To connect with young voters, the opposition is launching a major youth outreach campaign, including an upcoming gathering for women students in Pune to highlight issues concerning the nation's youth and social fabric.

7. RIZWAN ARSHAD TERMS DELIMITATION 'UNFAIR', WARNS SOUTH MAY BECOME 'TAX SLAVES' AT SOUTHERN CMS MEET
A special regional report highlights major political, economic, and civic developments across Southern Indian states. At the Southern Chief Ministers' meeting chaired by the Union Home Minister in Mahabalipuram, Karnataka Food and Civil Supplies Minister Rizwan Arshad criticized the proposed delimitation exercise. Arshad endorsed Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's resolution to freeze Lok Sabha seats at 543 based on the 1971 census, raising concerns over reduced tax devolution despite Southern states contributing 33 percent to India's GDP. Representatives from Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh addressed critical state priorities, including inter-state water disputes over the Cauvery and Mekedatu rivers, NEET, and federal fund allocation.

8. 31ST SOUTHERN ZONAL COUNCIL MEETS: FOCUS ON BULLET TRAIN CORRIDOR, WATER ISSUES AND WOMEN'S QUOTA
The 31st Southern Zonal Council meeting brought together Chief Ministers and representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Puducherry, Andaman and Nicobar, and Lakshadweep to address critical interstate and centre-state matters. Key discussions revolved around enhancing regional cooperation, developing transport infrastructure, and resolving longstanding interstate disputes. Proposals were introduced for a bullet train corridor connecting Amaravati, Bengaluru, and Chennai, alongside the interlinking of the Godavari and Cauvery rivers to mitigate ongoing water sharing conflicts.

9. AMIT SHAH CHAIRS SOUTH ZONAL MEET: DELIMITATION, WATER SHARING & RAIL LINKS TAKE CENTRE STAGE
First images have emerged from the Southern Zonal Council meeting chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah alongside key southern chief ministers and union territory representatives. Discussions focused on crucial interstate concerns including delimitation, water sharing, trade, and transport connectivity. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu highlighted the need for improved rail infrastructure and bullet train links between southern capital cities.

10. TN CM RAISES NEET EXEMPTION AND DELIMITATION ISSUES IN MEETING WITH HOME MINISTER AMIT SHAH
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister meets Union Home Minister Amit Shah at the Southern Zonal Council meeting to address major policy concerns. The Chief Minister calls for a NEET exemption in Tamil Nadu, proposing that MBBS, BDS, and AYUSH admissions be handled separately.

Source: India Today (indiatoday.in/india) - Date: August 20, 2026
